listing.name: Call to Power II / Apolyton Edition
listing.summary: Play your copy of Call to Power II with the Apolyton community edition.

restrictions.explanation: The community packages include game assets whose distribution terms still need review. Use the setup guide with a copy you’re entitled to use. Portcove can offer downloads once the exact package contents are cleared.

steps.title: Keep an untouched copy of the original
steps.instruction: Make a separate writable copy of your complete Call to Power II installation. Keep your original and your original saves. The Apolyton Edition needs data from the original game.

steps.title: Set up the Windows overlay
steps.instruction: Follow the release’s Apolyton_README.txt to overlay the community edition on the separate copy. Open ctp2_program/ctp/ctp2.exe from its folder. This is a 32-bit Windows program. If using the Chinese edition, follow the release notes for its data-directory and language settings.

steps.title: Prepare a Linux copy
steps.instruction: For a Linux source build, follow the upstream guide using data from your own game. Copy the map-generation libraries as directed and run ./ctp2 from ctp2_code/ctp. The release’s Debian package contains an x64 player under /opt/ctp2 and needs libavcodec59, libavformat59 and libswscale6. It still needs the original game files and a civpaths.txt configuration.

steps.title: Keep saves before changing versions
steps.instruction: Keep the active program folder’s save directory and back up any saves before opening copies in Apolyton. The release instructions say to enter /reloadslic in the game chat once after loading each older save. The upstream Linux guide links a separate converter for old Linux-format saves.

warnings: The Apolyton Edition is a community project. Activision did not make or support it.
